answer: After each lava flow reaches the sea the harbour surveys the new coastline and updates the chart, marking every yard of new land. A signal coastline drawn from an old chart fails the survey: at the shale of the delta the shore must match the flow's own rock, and an old chart shows water where land now stands. Forging a coastline takes a survey boat, a crew and 29,400 in vessel time, and the kernel chart in the harbour office is kept until the next flow, so a coast whose survey was never made is left uncharted.
